findings.description: Critical: D7 promises the run directory is derivable from the ledger header values, but D8 appends `-2`, `-3`, etc. on collisions without recording that suffix in the ledger. Two audits in the same UTC second at the same `HEAD` can therefore have header values that derive the unsuffixed path while the actual second ledger lives at a suffixed path.
findings.resolution: Either remove or qualify the derivability invariant in D7/proposal wording, or make collision disambiguation part of the recorded derivation. Since the plan's non-goals forbid schema/header changes, the narrow fix is to state that only the base run id is header-derived and collision suffixes are filesystem disambiguators, then align task assertions with that contract.

findings.description: Nit: D8's uniqueness guard is only specified and tested for an existing active run directory. Because retention moves old runs to `openspec/choices/archive/<run-id>/`, the active path can disappear while the archived destination still exists; a later audit with the same computed run id could reuse the active name and then collide with the archive destination on retention.
findings.resolution: Specify that the routing helper checks both `openspec/choices/<run-id>/` and `openspec/choices/archive/<run-id>/` when choosing suffixes, and add a task 4.1 or 5.2 assertion that a pre-existing archived run id forces the next suffix before retention runs.
